newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli analysts mixed on unchanged lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Israeli analysts mixed on unchanged lending rate.

text.p: Israeli market analysts were mixed in their reaction on Monday to the Bank of Israel's announcement that it was holding its key lending rate unchanged at 15.2 percent for December.

"I think that the market will be a bit disappointed, but okay, that's life. People don't expect a big, dramatic reduction until the budget is cut," said Doron Tsur, head of research for Sahar Securities.
"The direction, I think, is reduction but the pace is very slow. Not this month, so maybe next month," Tsur said.

Amitay Tafla at Sigma Securities said: "The central bank left the interest rate unchanged in order to press the government to cut the budget. The bank might be planning a substantial cut as part of a package deal that will include a sharp cut in spending."
"The decision is expected to have a negative impact on trading as investors were waiting for a cut of 0.2 to 0.3 percentage point," Tafla said.
"In the forex trading we saw an immediate reaction and the shekel started rising against the dollar. The Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq were also falling following the announcement," Tafla added.
